newsitem.title: USA: Spielberg's "Jurassic" sequel enjoys bronto opening. [CORRECTED 19:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Spielberg's "Jurassic" sequel enjoys bronto opening. [CORRECTED 19:50 GMT]

text.p: Steven Spielberg's dinosaurs trampled box office records during Memorial Day weekend as "The Lost World: Jurassic Park" opened with an estimated $90.1 million for the four-day period, according to studio estimates issued on Monday.

Including Thursday night previews in selected cities, the film's total haul rises to $92.7 million, giving it an estimated share of almost 70 percent of the total box office, according to Exhibitor Relations Co., which collects studios' estimates.
The special effects extravaganza kicked off a busy summer movie season full of mega-budgeted releases by establishing a slew of new benchmarks.
Its four-day total beats the previous record held by "Mission: Impossible," which earned $56.8 million for the Friday to Monday period of the Memorial Day holiday last year.
Its three-day total (Friday to Sunday and including Thursday previews) of $75.0 million beats the $52.78 million that 1995's "Batman Forever" earned during its first three days.
Additionally, the film's $22 million opening on Friday beats the $20.1 million opening for "Batman Forever."

Exhibitor Relations predicted the film would pass $100 million on Tuesday, its fifth day of release, making it the fastest film to reach that mark. The record is currently held by "Independence Day," which took seven days in 1996.
"We certainly had some big expectations, but it's hard to predict anything would become a phenomenon of these proportions," said a spokesman for Universal Pictures, which released the film.
Universal is a unit of Canada's Seagram Co. Ltd..

By contrast, "Jurassic Park," the film's predecessor, earned $50.2 million in its first three days (including Thursday night previews), when it opened in June 1993. It ended up with $357.1 million at the domestic box office.

"The Lost World: Jurassic Park" features Jeff Goldblum, returning from the original, Julianne Moore, Vince Vaughn and Pete Postlethwaite, who battle raging raptors and evil capitalists in a loose adaptation of novelist Michael Crichton's "The Lost World." But the real stars are the dinosaurs -- bigger, faster and hungrier than before -- and the film's special effects team.

The film opened in 3,281 theatres, and averaged $21,061 per screen. It carries a reported budget of $80 million, a bargain by the standards of upcoming movies such as the $90 million "Men In Black" and the rumoured $200 million for "Titanic," whose scheduled summer release reportedly looks set to be delayed until the end of the year.

The No. 2 movie at the weekend box office was the Meg Ryan romantic comedy "Addicted To Love," which opened with an estimated $12.1 million for the four days. The Bruce Willis sci-fi picture, "The Fifth Element," which held the top spot for the previous two weekends, slipped to third with $8.2 million. (Corrects numbers for "Addicted To Love" and "The Fifth Element")
